query: Why have I become so cynical?

per_question.q: Which page leaves the reader more in charge of changing this?
per_question.why: By placing the seminar link outside the identify-box, Page A lets the self-identification box stand purely as the reader's self-assessment without immediately monetizing their recognition.

per_question.q: Which page asks less of the reader before it has earned it?
per_question.why: Page B prematurely embeds a paid seminar pitch directly inside the introductory identification box before the reader has even left the opening callout.

per_question.q: Which page treats the reader as the person who does the work, rather than as someone who has to be sent somewhere?
per_question.why: Page A keeps the punchline of the identify-box ('Run those as a standing policy...') as the concluding takeaway, rather than immediately handing the reader off to an off-site seminar link as in B.

per_question.q: Which page gives the reader more room to decide for themselves what to do next?
per_question.why: Page A separates the callout box content from the outbound seminar link, leaving the core diagnostic exercise self-contained.

per_question.q: Which page puts the author's own history to better use for the reader?
per_question.why: The personal history section is identical on both pages, but Page A frames the journey cleanly without having pushed commercial seminar attendance inside the early recognition box.

per_question.q: Which page makes the first screen feel more like the reader's own words?
per_question.why: Page B dilutes the four self-diagnostic statements by terminating the identify-box with a promotional link to a seminar rather than the reader's internal monologue.

per_question.q: Which page's opening is easier to read straight through without being interrupted?
per_question.why: Page B places the seminar link cleanly inside the styled identify-box container rather than leaving a standalone, uncontained link dangling right above the opening narrative hook.

per_question.q: Which page makes a reader likelier to think "that is me" in the first thirty seconds?
per_question.why: The identify-box in Page A finishes with the psychological consequence ('and the cost is a read on people that no person can change') rather than pivoting to an advertisement.

per_question.q: Which page keeps its argument moving without a detour that breaks the thread?
per_question.why: Page A preserves the identify-box as a unified rhetorical unit that sets up the problem cleanly before presenting an optional external link.

per_question.q: Which page makes it easier to follow the line from the question at the top to the answer?
per_question.why: The progression from the short answer to the internal self-talk quotes flows without being interrupted from within the box by seminar marketing.

A: Leaves the seminar link sitting as an unadorned paragraph directly between the callout box and the opening narrative hook.
B: Contaminates the identify-box by tucking a commercial seminar offer directly under personal self-reflection quotes.

first_screen: Page A leaves the reader more in charge because the identify-box completes its psychological insight without immediately trying to capture the user inside a seminar container.
provenance: Both pages are completely identical in empirical citations and literature provenance; Page A slightly edges out Page B by keeping promotional seminar links distinct from the analytical text.
